Suez Canal traffic backs up as ship stays stuck

Queues of vessels waiting to transit the Suez Canal grew on Friday as salvage crews struggled to move the grounded container ship.

A spokesperson for the Suez Canal Authority said: "Every effort is being made to reopen the waterway as quickly as possible."

Shipping companies warned that the disruption would add days to Asia-Europe voyages, and some carriers were weighing a diversion around the Cape of Good Hope, which adds roughly ten days to the journey.

Insurers said the grounding was the most serious canal blockage in several years, and port operators in Europe were preparing for a surge of arrivals once traffic resumes.
